summary: Execution covered 11 experiments in 10.2 minutes; 5 carried compute-bound labels. Qwen3.6 direct baseline headroom qualification was the longest compute entry, the locked compute-task idle assessment is false, and the records lack causal phase timing and model-concurrency fields.
bottlenecks_identified: Qwen3.6 direct baseline headroom qualification took 3.68 minutes and Gemma 4 26B-A4B direct baseline headroom qualification took 1.1 minutes. For the reason behind either duration, no data available this milestone.
The point-in-time GPU report cannot grade accelerator use across all 5 compute-bound experiments or establish whether another ready experiment could have used the available device capacity.
The closeout evidence omits loaded-model count and runner-selection receipts, so DualGPURunner eligibility cannot be audited.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic task and phase clocks together with task-linked accelerator samples for every compute-bound experiment.
Add a readiness-aware scheduler that can place independent single-model experiments on separate available GPUs while retaining one GPU per single-model task.
Persist loaded-model count, device assignment, and runner choice at launch so DualGPURunner is selected and auditable only for parallel multi-model work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Schedule ready independent single-model experiments across available GPUs.
Capture task-scoped phase clocks and accelerator telemetry.
Emit model-count, device-assignment, and runner-selection receipts at launch.
meta_reflection: The GPU sample shows strong engagement on the active device, so it does not support a compute-task idle defect; spare device capacity instead motivates a conditional cross-experiment scheduling test. The 11% estimate is 1.1 divided by 10.2, rounded, and assumes the named compute streams were ready to overlap; the records provide no concurrent-model launch receipt with which to judge DualGPURunner.
